comparator.name: Art History
comparator.sourceNotes: The current Leiden Study Guide lists two 180 EC formal routes. Arts and Culture is the broad historical route for the generic Art History target. Year one comprises 60 EC of required courses. Year two comprises 40 EC of required courses, one 5 EC seminar in each semester and one 10 EC excursion. The selected Art I and Art II seminars require Visual Analysis and Academic Skills II. The Florence excursion additionally requires a completed second-year seminar. Year three comprises 10 EC of required research and publishing study, one 10 EC seminar, the 10 EC final paper and 30 EC of open electives. The selected architectural preservation seminar requires the first year and both second-year seminars. The current Aesthetics course replaces the older module named in the research methods prerequisite. The final paper requires the first year, both second-year seminars and Perspectives on Art Historical Research. The ordinary final-paper offering is in the second semester. First-semester entry requires board approval.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names generic Art History, not Arts, Media and Society. Leiden’s current official curriculum offers those two formal 180-EC routes. Arts and Culture spans the historical art and architecture periods, material study, museums, heritage, theory, methods and research that define the broad Art History identity; it is selected on that academic basis, before UCR course selection.

core: European art history from antiquity through the early modern and modern periods, with analysis of painting, sculpture and architecture
Material culture, architectural form and the making of objects
Global and cross-regional art history, including Africa and the Americas
Museums, collecting, display, cultural heritage and the interpretation of artworks
Visual analysis, art-historical methods, evidence-based interpretation and the historiography of art
Historical and social contexts of art and culture across periods
Art-historical seminars, research and independent final paper
adjacent: Contemporary art, media and society as an official alternative within Leiden Art History, connecting visual culture, digital media and social questions
Communication, representation and cultural meaning in modern visual and audiovisual media
questions: How do museums and heritage institutions select, display and interpret art?
How do contemporary images, media and artistic practices shape public understanding of society and global issues?

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

Examines African artistic traditions and heritage, extending the historical art curriculum beyond Europe.

alternatives.label: Art, Heritage and Historical Cultures
alternatives.labelReason: Eight art, archaeology and heritage courses anchor the historical route. Courses in history, literature, visual media, philosophy and research extend its methods and context.
alternatives.concept: Studies art and objects across periods and regions through art history, archaeology, museum studies and heritage. Historical inquiry, myths and literature provide context for interpreting objects and images. Ethics and the philosophy of emotion add ways to examine how people experience and judge art and heritage.
progression: Personal & Professional Development and introductory Western art history are in the first semester. Art, material culture, historical and media foundations lead into advanced museum study, art historiography and source-based historical inquiry.

alternatives.label: Contemporary Art, Media and Society
alternatives.labelReason: Six art, archaeology and heritage courses and six media courses anchor a study of contemporary visual representation. Communication and sociology add ways to study persuasion, public debate and the social contexts of images.
alternatives.concept: Examines how art, film, television and digital media shape public debate and representation. Art history and museum study give a historical base. Courses in environmental media, race and representation, rhetoric and sociology examine how images and messages circulate and whose perspectives they convey.
alternatives.distinctness: Nine courses (67.5 EC) differ in each direction. This option adds television and digital media, environmental representation, climate communication, persuasion and social theory. The historical option gives that space to history, ancient material culture, myths and literature, and philosophy of emotion.
progression: Personal & Professional Development, introductory Western art history, film and media, and sociology are in the first semester. These foundations support later work in visual representation, public communication, art historiography and social theory.

selection.assessment: The historical option integrates the nine broad Art History interests through direct study of painting, objects, global art, museums and disciplinary methods, with narrower architectural and design coverage. The formal Arts, Media and Society direction supports a substantively different contemporary option. A standalone architecture/design or museum direction would require sustained specialist study beyond the available courses. The illustrative and career interests do not support further concepts.

blocks: Leiden requires a digital humanities course. UCR studies digital and physical media across several courses.
Art history, visual objects and historical contexts
Both build close observation of artworks and use visual evidence to support an argument. UCR focuses on paintings. Leiden also uses architecture, decorative art and photography.
Both ask how materials and making inform the interpretation of objects. UCR concentrates on ancient craft and archaeology, while Leiden treats techniques in art and architecture.
Both treat artistic traditions outside Europe and their interpretation across cultures. UCR focuses on African art, including collecting and repatriation.
Both study Renaissance visual art and architecture in their wider historical setting. UCR focuses on Italy and its trading and cultural connections.
UCR’s Western art survey includes painting from this period. Leiden gives 1550–1800 dedicated attention and connects European works to a wider global setting.
UCR develops argument and source skills in rhetoric and historical research. Leiden introduces the specific sources and conventions of art history.
UCR includes an art-history course paper and a later history research paper. Leiden has a dedicated first-year course on writing art-historical research.
UCR studies ancient Greek archaeology and civic material culture. Leiden spans art and architecture from antiquity through the medieval period.
UCR’s literature courses help interpret myths and narratives. Leiden teaches a dedicated method for identifying and interpreting subjects and symbols in artworks.

UCR addresses aesthetic interpretation in art historiography and studies artistic emotion in the historical option. Leiden gives aesthetics a dedicated course and applies it to a museum or exhibition visit.
Leiden applies visual analysis and research writing in a dedicated art-history seminar. UCR develops these skills in its art and history courses.
Leiden’s selected seminar uses recent scholarship to examine Renaissance art and exchange. UCR studies this subject in its Renaissance art course, which is paired with Leiden’s period survey.
Leiden includes a supervised excursion seminar in Florence. UCR studies Renaissance art and architecture in class.
UCR studies Renaissance architecture and artefacts. Leiden follows architecture and design in Europe and the US through the modern period.
UCR includes modern art and exhibition study. Leiden surveys European and US visual art from 1800 onward through movements, media and themes.
Both analyse recent art through themes and its relationship to museums. UCR focuses on modern art and exhibition strategies, while Leiden gives more attention to contemporary art around the world.
Both examine the formation of art history as a discipline and its changing methods of interpretation.
UCR studies modern exhibitions and the collection of African art. Leiden traces museums from early modern collecting to national institutions.
UCR studies historic buildings and material culture. Leiden’s selected seminar focuses on architectural preservation as a creative practice.
UCR studies ancient civic heritage and the provenance of African art. Leiden also teaches heritage documentation, archives and preservation tools.
Social theory, communication and cultural research
UCR practises historical research and studies the methods of art historians. Leiden uses a dedicated course to prepare for the Art History final paper.
Leiden teaches academic publication as a distinct part of the degree. UCR develops writing and research through course assignments.
Leiden requires an independent Art History final paper. UCR’s optional independent research sits outside the displayed 180 EC schedule.
Leiden leaves these 15 EC open for elective study in the first semester of year three.
Leiden leaves these 15 EC open for elective study in the second semester of year three.

notes.text: Leiden requires a longer sequence in art history, with dedicated work in architecture and design, aesthetics, museum history and heritage methods. It also requires specialist seminars, an excursion and an Art History final paper. UCR combines its art and heritage courses with history, media and related methods.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s Arts and Culture route studies painting, sculpture, architecture and design from antiquity to the present. It combines close analysis of artworks with global art history, museum and heritage studies, aesthetics and art-historical research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: At UCR, you can focus on art and heritage across periods or on contemporary visual culture and its social contexts. The historical option combines art history and archaeology with museum and heritage study. The contemporary option gives more space to film, media, communication and sociology.

curriculum.limitation: This example uses two medieval and early modern art seminars, a Florence excursion seminar and a third-year architectural preservation seminar. The third year includes 30 EC of open electives. The Art History final paper normally follows the first year, both second-year seminars and Perspectives on Art Historical Research.
